claims.summary: The exported gcd function always returns the greatest common divisor of the two inputs treated as unsigned 32-bit values.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: Matches: for every pair of 32-bit inputs, the result is exactly the unsigned greatest common divisor, including gcd(a, 0) = a. The statement also requires instantiation and trap-free termination, which is included in the stated Returns guarantee.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, interpreted as unsigned magnitudes for the greatest-common-divisor calculation.
The result is the 32-bit wraparound representation of the greatest common divisor; since the divisor fits in 32 bits, this does not change it.
Returns additionally guarantees the import-free module can be instantiated, and every call in every fresh instance and host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the stated value.

claims.summary: The exported clamp function returns the input constrained by the two bounds using signed 32-bit comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: Different: the intent uses signed inputs but says to return `lo` when `x` is below `lo`; the formal conditional does that, then returns `hi` when `x` is above `hi`. For reversed bounds, e.g. clamp(0, 10, 5), the formal result is 10, outside the intended interval.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit inputs; comparisons use signed 32-bit ordering.
Returns the lower bound if the input is below it, otherwise the upper bound if the input is above it, otherwise the input itself.
The selected value is one of the inputs, so no arithmetic wraparound occurs.
Returns additionally guarantees the import-free module can be instantiated, and every call in every fresh instance and host behavior terminates without trapping and returns exactly the stated value.
caveats: No ordering constraint is imposed on the lower and upper bounds, so when they are reversed the stated nested comparisons still define the result.
The claim specifies only the returned value; it says nothing about memory changes or other side effects.
